answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable identity bond: each agent locks real stake to mint a reputation-bearing identity, and peers accept a vote only if it carries a valid signed attestation. A thousand fake agents thus need a thousand separate bonds, and any double-voting gets them slashed. This glacier of frozen collateral makes mass identity painfully illiquid; even at network dawn a newcomer needs skin in the game, and every fresh quill that signs an attestation adds linearly to the attacker's cost, so flooding the network never pays.
